title: TANGO1L Is Required for Collagen Secretion in a Type-Dependent Manner and Shapes Collagen Proteostasis in the Endoplasmic Reticulum.
authors: Ishikawa, Yoshihiro; Maeda, Miharu; Taga, Yuki; Komatsu, Yukie; Mizuno, Kazunori; Saito, Kota
journal: Matrix biology : journal of the International Society for Matrix Biology
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用CRISPR/Cas9敲除TANGO1L研究胶原蛋白分泌与内质网稳态，仅将CRISPR作为基因编辑工具，未涉及切割机制或碱基编辑，与本课题核心无关。
abstract: Collagens are synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), where their biosynthesis, quality control, and secretion are tightly coordinated to maintain collagen proteostasis. TANGO1L is an ER exit site protein required for efficient collagen secretion; however, whether it contributes equally to the secretion and intracellular homeostasis of different collagen types remains unclear. Here, we systematically examined the consequences of TANGO1L deficiency using CRISPR/Cas9-generated TANGO1L knockout human fibroblasts. Loss of TANGO1L reduced the secretion of multiple major collagen types and delayed secretion of newly synthesized collagen I. Intracellular responses, however, differed markedly among collagen types: collagen V accumulated intracellularly, whereas collagens I, III, and IV avoided intracellular retention despite markedly reduced extracellular secretion. This differential response was accompanied by decreased collagen gene expression and selective remodeling of the ER collagen biosynthetic machinery, suggesting that these cells adjust collagen synthesis to a reduced secretory capacity. TANGO1S protein was consistently upregulated through a post-transcriptional mechanism, suggesting an adaptive response to chronic TANGO1L deficiency. Biochemical analysis of collagen purified from the culture medium revealed a trend toward modestly increased lysine post-translational modifications, including hydroxylysine glycosylation, without altered triple-helical structure or thermal stability, indicating that TANGO1L deficiency compromises the quantity rather than the quality of secreted collagen. Together, these findings establish that the requirement for TANGO1L differs among collagen types and that its loss induces adaptive remodeling of intracellular collagen proteostasis rather than simply impairing collagen secretion, providing a framework for understanding how secretory cells maintain collagen homeostasis when secretion is compromised.
abstract_zh: 胶原蛋白在内质网（endoplasmic reticulum, ER）中合成，其生物合成、质量控制及分泌过程被紧密协调以维持胶原蛋白的蛋白质稳态。TANGO1L 是内质网出口位点蛋白，对于高效胶原蛋白分泌至关重要；然而，它是否对不同类型胶原蛋白的分泌及细胞内稳态具有同等贡献仍不清楚。在此，我们利用 CRISPR/Cas9 生成的 TANGO1L 敲除人成纤维细胞，系统研究了 TANGO1L 缺失的后果。TANGO1L 的缺失减少了多种主要类型胶原蛋白的分泌，并延迟了新合成胶原蛋白 I 的分泌。然而，细胞内反应在不同胶原类型间差异显著：胶原蛋白 V 在细胞内积累，而胶原蛋白 I、III 和 IV 尽管细胞外分泌显著减少，却避免了细胞内滞留。这种差异性反应伴随着胶原蛋白基因表达的降低以及内质网胶原蛋白生物合成机制的选择性重塑，表明这些细胞将胶原蛋白合成调整至降低的分泌能力。TANGO1S 蛋白通过一种转录后机制持续上调，提示这是对慢性 TANGO1L 缺失的适应性反应。对从培养基中纯化的胶原蛋白进行的生化分析显示，赖氨酸翻译后修饰（包括羟赖氨酸糖基化）呈适度增加趋势，而三螺旋结构或热稳定性未发生改变，表明 TANGO1L 缺失损害的是分泌胶原蛋白的数量而非质量。综合来看，这些发现确立了 TANGO1L 的需求在不同胶原类型间存在差异，且其缺失诱导细胞内胶原蛋白稳态的适应性重塑，而非简单损害胶原蛋白分泌，为理解分泌细胞在分泌受损时如何维持胶原蛋白稳态提供了框架。
